thread:
maria: Heads-up — trying to reconcile SM occupancy vs queue-depth signals for hosted vs dedicated pools. we need a clear metric set before the next console rollout.

sam: +1. can we start with names + retention/aggregation plan? current dashboards are noisy.

jia: thinking of three core timeseries: sm_occupancy (slots used / slots total), memory_used_bytes, queue_depth_slots. low-cardinality labels only.

tom: agree on core metrics but we have concerns about cardinality from labels like instance_id or job_id. need sampling or rollup.

maria: proposal: export per-pool, per-allocator, and per-device labels only. avoid per-request labels. keep instance_id out of high-retention series.

anita: on Dedicated we also care about tenant_id for billing. could we have a separate billing stream with stronger RBAC?

sam: yes separate stream for billing/chargeback. that stream can be higher-cardinality and sampled to 1m and TTL 30d. public telemetry stays 5m rollups, 90d aggregate.

jia: rough prometheus names + promql suggestions:
```
# raw-ish 1m series (ingested into tsdb)
redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy{pool="hosted",pool_type="shared"} 0.67
redwood_gpu_memory_used_bytes{device="a100",pool="dedicated"} 1234567890
redwood_gpu_queue_depth_slots{pool="hosted"} 12

# console panels use 5m avg + p95
avg_over_time(redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy[5m])
quantile_over_time(0.95, redwood_gpu_memory_used_bytes[5m])
```

maria: love the examples. two questions: 1) how to handle spikebursts where queue depth jumps for seconds (alerts) vs long tail (dashboard)? 2) who owns alert thresholds?

sam: for spikes we suggest event-driven sampling: keep a 1s heartbeat metric for queue_depth_peak which is ingested into a short-term hot-store for 1h and then aggregated into 5m rollup. alerts read the hot-store.

tom: implementation note: hot-store will be a new Kafka topic + consumer -> hot TSDB. needs infra changes and onboarding plan. i can spin up proto consumer but need schema.

jia: schema draft (flat, low-cardinality labels):
```json
{
  "metric": "redwood_gpu_queue_depth_slots",
  "labels": ["pool","pool_type","device"],
  "value": 12,
  "ts": 1612345678000
}
```

anita: pinging product for dashboard UX: we need a single "GPU Pool" card that toggles hosted/dedicated and changes aggregation config.

maria: product/console: can we expose a small help tooltip: "why hosted shows higher p95 queue depth — due to multi-tenant batching". helps SRE + customers.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: telemetry-ingester v2 -> staging (sha: a1b2c3).

sam: FYI — this will change the cost profile of the ingest pipeline. we should add quota guardrails so free-tier users don't blow up costs by enabling high-cardinality billing streams.

maria: action items:
- tom: prototype hot-store consumer + schema (ETA: 48h)
- sam: quota + sampling policy draft for billing stream (ETA: 72h)
- jia: prom metric names + example panels for console (ETA: 24h)
- anita: product copy + UX mock for pool toggle (ETA: 5d)
- maria: write short runbook for alert ownership and thresholds (ETA: 3d)

jia: quick note: p95 vs p99 decisions matter. for hosted we care p95 latency/backpressure; for Dedicated tenants p99 might be more appropriate. include both in panels.

maria: also decide retention: raw 1m hot-store 1h, 1m raw -> 7d cold, 5m rollups -> 90d. ok?

sam: ok but we should add 30d export for customers on Dedicated (s3).

tom: i'm adding a proto schema PR to git now. will tag this thread.

anita: thanks all — this feels actionable. I'll schedule a 30m sync next week to go over UX + alerts. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks everyone. please add any follow-ups to the PR or ping me. :thumbsup:
